    42	
    43	# Lean file path under the project. ``:LINE`` suffix captured when present.
    44	# The outer ``(?:/…)*`` also matches the root ``MIPStarRE.lean`` file.  A
    45	# leading ``\b`` keeps the match from starting mid-identifier.
    46	_FILE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(MIPStarRE(?:/[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+)*\.lean)(?::(\d+))?")
    47	
    48	# GitHub blob URLs often appear in issue bodies; normalize them to plain
    49	# ``MIPStarRE/...`` citations before scanning so we don't greedily match the
    50	# repo-name prefix (``.../MIPStarRE/blob/main/...``) as part of the path.
    51	_GITHUB_BLOB_RE = re.compile(
    52	    r"https?://github\.com/[^/\s]+/[^/\s]+/blob/[^\s#]+?/"
    53	    r"(MIPStarRE(?:/[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+)*\.lean)(?:#L(\d+)(?:-L\d+)?)?"
    54	)
    55	
    56	# "line 141" / "Line 131" — used when a path is mentioned nearby without the
    57	# bare ``:LINE`` suffix (the common table-cell idiom in this repo's issues).
    58	_LINE_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"\bline\s+(\d{1,6})\b", re.IGNORECASE)
    59	
    60	# Backtick-quoted token that looks like a Lean identifier.  Deliberately
    61	# conservative: must start with a letter, minimum two chars, only identifier
    62	# punctuation allowed.  This filters out inline prose like `main` and `sorry`
    63	# via the _DECL_STOPLIST below rather than by regex alone.
    64	_BACKTICK_DECL_RE = re.compile(r"`([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.']{1,})`")
    65	
    66	# Declaration-definition pattern used to build the "known declarations" set.
    67	# Matches the header line of a Lean declaration; mirrors the lighter-weight
    68	# variant used by scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py but only returns the short
    69	# (unqualified) name.
    70	_DECL_DEFN_RE = re.compile(
    71	    r"^\s*(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?"
    72	    r"(?:(?:noncomputable|protected|private|local)\s+)*"
    73	    r"(?:def|theorem|lemma|abbrev|instance|class|structure|inductive|opaque)\s+"
    74	    r"([A-Za-z_][\w.']*)",
    75	    re.MULTILINE,
    76	)

    78	_NAMESPACE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*namespace\s+([A-Za-z_][\w.']*)\b")
    79	_END_NAMESPACE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*end(?:\s+([A-Za-z_][\w.']*))?\s*(?:--.*)?$")

    81	# Sorry markers we count as "still unproven".
    82	_SORRY_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(sorry|admit)\b")

    84	# Tokens that are common English words, Lean keywords, or otherwise too
    85	# ambiguous to treat as declaration citations.  Any backtick token in this
    86	# set is skipped.
    87	_DECL_STOPLIST = frozenset({
    88	    "sorry", "admit", "main", "by", "true", "false", "Prop", "Type",
    89	    "True", "False", "Nat", "Int", "Rat", "Real", "Complex",
    90	    "rfl", "simp", "rw", "exact", "apply", "intro", "cases",
    91	    "this", "self", "it", "foo", "bar", "baz", "qux",

    93	    "lean", "lake", "gh", "git", "rg", "grep", "sed", "awk",
    94	    "python", "python3", "bash", "sh", "ls", "cd",
    95	})

   136	def _normalize_github_blob_urls(body: str) -> str:
   137	    """Rewrite GitHub blob URLs to plain ``MIPStarRE/...[:LINE]`` citations."""
   138	
   139	    def repl(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
   140	        path = match.group(1)
   141	        line = match.group(2)
   142	        return f"{path}:{line}" if line is not None else path
   143	
   144	    return _GITHUB_BLOB_RE.sub(repl, body)

   147	def extract_file_citations(body: str) -> list[FileCitation]:
   148	    """Pull ``MIPStarRE/.../file.lean[:LINE]`` references out of ``body``.
   149	
   150	    When the path appears in a table row that separately lists ``line NNN``
   151	    (the common convention in sorry-site trackers), we attach the nearest
   152	    ``line NNN`` on the same line as the path.
   153	    """
   154	    out: list[FileCitation] = []
   155	    for raw_line in _normalize_github_blob_urls(body).splitlines():
   156	        paths_on_line = list(_FILE_RE.finditer(raw_line))
   157	        if not paths_on_line:
   158	            continue
   159	        line_hints = [int(m.group(1)) for m in _LINE_WORD_RE.finditer(raw_line)]
   160	        for idx, m in enumerate(paths_on_line):
   161	            path = m.group(1)
   162	            if m.group(2) is not None:
   163	                out.append(FileCitation(path=path, line=int(m.group(2))))
   164	                continue
   165	            # No ``:LINE`` suffix — fall back to a ``line NNN`` word on the
   166	            # same line only when exactly one path appears (avoids cross
   167	            # attribution in tables with multiple rows on one wrapped line).
   168	            if len(paths_on_line) == 1 and len(line_hints) == 1:
   169	                out.append(FileCitation(path=path, line=line_hints[0]))
   170	            else:
   171	                out.append(FileCitation(path=path, line=None))
   172	    # Deduplicate while preserving order.
   173	    seen: set[tuple[str, int | None]] = set()
   174	    unique: list[FileCitation] = []
   175	    for fc in out:
   176	        key = (fc.path, fc.line)
   177	        if key in seen:
   178	            continue
   179	        seen.add(key)
   180	        unique.append(fc)
   181	    return unique

   183	
   184	def extract_decl_citations(body: str) -> list[DeclCitation]:
   185	    """Pull backtick-quoted Lean-identifier-shaped tokens out of ``body``."""
   186	    out: list[DeclCitation] = []
   187	    seen: set[str] = set()
   188	    for m in _BACKTICK_DECL_RE.finditer(body):
   189	        name = m.group(1)
   190	        if name in _DECL_STOPLIST or name in seen:
   191	            continue
   192	        # Require at least one lowercase or digit; purely uppercase backtick
   193	        # items are dropped, which helps exclude obvious sentence starts like
   194	        # `The`.  This is a soft filter.
   195	        if not any(c.islower() or c.isdigit() for c in name):
   196	            continue
   197	        seen.add(name)
   198	        out.append(DeclCitation(name=name))
   199	    return out

   206	def build_decl_index(lean_root: Path) -> set[str]:
   207	    """Collect declaration names under ``lean_root``.
   208	
   209	    The index stores both short names (for unqualified issue citations) and the
   210	    namespace-qualified names visible from simple ``namespace ...`` blocks.  A
   211	    cited qualified name is later matched exactly, so ``Foo.bar`` cannot be
   212	    silently satisfied by some unrelated short declaration named ``bar``.
   213	    """
   214	    names: set[str] = set()
   215	    for path in sorted(lean_root.rglob("*.lean")):
   216	        try:
   217	            text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
   218	        except OSError:
   219	            continue
   220	        namespace_stack: list[str] = []
   221	        for line in text.splitlines():
   222	            if m := _NAMESPACE_RE.match(line):
   223	                namespace_stack.extend(m.group(1).split("."))
   224	                continue
   225	            if m := _END_NAMESPACE_RE.match(line):
   226	                end_name = m.group(1)
   227	                if end_name:
   228	                    parts = end_name.split(".")
   229	                    if namespace_stack[-len(parts):] == parts:
   230	                        del namespace_stack[-len(parts):]
   231	                    # Otherwise this is likely closing a named section, not a
   232	                    # tracked namespace; leave the namespace stack unchanged.
   233	                # An anonymous ``end`` is ambiguous: in this repo it commonly
   234	                # closes an unnamed ``section`` inside a namespace.  Do not pop
   235	                # the namespace stack unless Lean text explicitly names the
   236	                # namespace being closed.
   237	                continue
   238	            if m := _DECL_DEFN_RE.match(line):
   239	                declared = m.group(1)
   240	                short = declared.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
   241	                names.add(short)
   242	                names.add(declared)
   243	                if namespace_stack:
   244	                    names.add(".".join([*namespace_stack, declared]))
   245	    return names

     7	fourth pin.  In a directory of markdown files nothing enforces any of it, which

     9	validator for parent-child symmetry and acyclicity, since frontmatter has no

   222	def _check_acyclic(issues: dict[str, track.Issue], findings: Findings) -> None:

   224	    state: dict[str, int] = {}  # 0 = visiting, 1 = done

   227	        if state.get(start) == 1:
   228	            continue

   230	        node: str | None = start
   231	        while node is not None and state.get(node) != 1:
   232	            if node in path:
   233	                cycle = path[path.index(node):] + [node]
   234	                findings.error(
   235	                    issues[node].path.name, "cycle",
   236	                    "parent chain forms a cycle: " + " -> ".join("#" + n for n in cycle),
   237	                )
   238	                break
   239	            path.append(node)
   240	            state[node] = 0
   241	            current = issues.get(node)
   242	            if current is None:
   243	                break
   244	            try:
   245	                node = current.parent
   246	            except LayerError:
   247	                break
   248	            if node is not None and node not in issues:
   249	                break
   250	        for node_id in path:
   251	            state[node_id] = 1

   174	## 7. Which reviews run
   175	
   176	* **Code review** always.  `pr-review.yml` ran it as a matrix over
   177	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` (anthropic, deepseek).  Locally the matrix

    32	In this section, we will survey two tools for doing so.
    33	The first of these is the textbook Naimark dilation theorem.
    34	In our setting, it states the following.
    35	
    36	\begin{theorem}[Naimark dilation]\label{thm:naimark}
    37	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
    38	Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{A}}$
    39	and $B=\{B^y_b\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
    40	Then there exists
    41	\begin{enumerate}
    42	\item Hilbert spaces $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$ and $\calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    43	\item a state $\ket{\mathsf{aux}} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    44	\item and two measurements  $\widehat{A} = \{\widehat{A}^x_a\}$ and $\widehat{B}=\{\widehat{B}^y_b\}$
    45	acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$
    46	and $\calH_{\mathrm{B}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$,
    47	respectively,
    48	\end{enumerate}
    49	such that the following is true.
    50	If we write $\ket{\widehat{\psi}} = \ket{\psi} \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}}$,
    51	then for all $x,y, a, b$,
    52	 \begin{equation*}
    53	 \bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}
    54	 = \bra{\widehat{\psi}} \widehat{A}^x_a \ot \widehat{B}^y_b \ket{\widehat{\psi}}.
    55	 \end{equation*}
    56	 In addition, $\ket{\mathsf{aux}}$ is a \emph{product state},
    57	 meaning that we can write it as
    58	 \begin{equation*}
    59	 \ket{\mathsf{aux}}= \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} \ot \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}},
    60	 \end{equation*}
    61	for $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$
    62	and $\ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}}$ in $\calH_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}}$.
    63	\end{theorem}
    64	The second of these is the ``orthogonalization lemma" from~\cite{KV11}.
    65	In the setting of symmetric strategies, it states the following.
    66	
    67	\begin{theorem}[Orthogonalization lemma]\label{thm:orthonormalization}
    68	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a permutation-invariant state,
    69	and let $A = \{A_a\}$ be a sub-measurement with strong self-consistency
    70	\begin{equation*}
    71	\sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes A_a \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\zeta.
    72	\end{equation*}
    73	Then there exists a projective sub-measurement $P = \{P_a\}$ such that
    74	\begin{equation*}
    75	A_a \otimes I \approx_{100 \zeta^{1/4}} P_a \otimes I.
    76	\end{equation*}
    77	\end{theorem}
    78	
    79	These two results serve largely the same purpose,
    80	and for our applications it will typically suffice to use either one.
    81	That said, there are tradeoffs when choosing to use one or the other.
    82	Naimark dilation is convenient because it can be applied to any family of sub-measurements
    83	and it preserves measurement outcome probabilities exactly.
    84	On the other hand, it requires swapping out the state $\ket{\psi}$ and measurements~$A$ and~$B$
    85	for $\ket{\widehat{\psi}}$ and $\widehat{A}$ and $\widehat{B}$, respectively,
    86	which can be notationally cumbersome.
    87	Most works opt to skip adding the hats,
    88	and instead say something to the effect of ``using Naimark, we can assume that~$A$ and~$B$ are projective."
    89	However, there is subtlety in doing so,
    90	which is that Naimark dilation does not necessarily preserve ``$\approx_{\delta}$" statements;
    91	in other words, $A^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$
    92	does not necessarily imply $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$.

    95	but $\widehat{A}^x_a \ot I \approx_{\delta} I \ot \widehat{B}^x_a$ only holds for $\delta \geq 1$.)

    98	(That said, as pointed out at the end of Section~$4.4$ of~\cite{NW19},
